findings.title: Same NPE remains in the paginated getSubGroupsStream overloads
findings.body: The fix null-guards only `getSubGroupsCount()`. The three paginated `getSubGroupsStream(...)` overloads (lines 256, 262, 268) still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` directly. `modelSupplier.get()` returns null when the group has been deleted in the database but the cached adapter is still in use. That is exactly the concurrent-deletion race this PR targets. Listing or paginating subgroups of a group deleted by another request will still throw a NullPointerException and return HTTP 500. These call sites should get the same null handling, e.g. return `Stream.empty()` when the model is null.

findings.title: Reader thread is never joined, so its exceptions can be missed
findings.body: The test sets `deletedAll` to true and then asserts on `caughtExceptions` right away, without joining the reader thread. At that moment the reader may still be inside a `groups()` request that overlapped the last deletions. An exception from that request is added to the list after the assertion has already passed, so a regression can go undetected. Nothing guarantees the reader issued any request during the deletion window either, so the test may pass without exercising the race at all. Keep a reference to the thread, `join()` it after setting the flag, and ideally check that at least one read overlapped the deletions.

findings.title: Background thread loops forever if a deletion throws
findings.body: `deletedAll.set(true)` runs only after every `remove()` call succeeds. If any deletion throws (e.g. a 500 or a 404), the flag is never set. The non-daemon reader thread then keeps calling the admin API in a tight loop indefinitely. It leaks into later tests and can keep the JVM from exiting. Put the deletion loop in try/finally so the flag is always set, and make the thread a daemon or join it.
